checks: No eclipse at 1 of 17 covered epochs where the 4.12025 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 389107837 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.120253 days and a primary eclipse depth of 15.20 percent. The star does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected the eclipse signal with high significance (signal-to-noise ratio of 126.8), and pixel-level imaging confirmed the signal at a signal-to-noise ratio of 20.7. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, indicating that the initially measured period was half the true orbital period. No secondary eclipse was detected. The machine-learning screening score of 0.46 suggests moderate confidence in this as a real target, and further investigation would be needed to fully characterize this system.
